text:
search index=`cs_index` sourcetype=crowdstrike:events:sensor earliest=-7d
  event_platform=Mac event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
  SigningId="com.apple.*"
  NOT (CsValidationCategory=1 TeamId="-")
| stats count as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen,
        values(SigningId) as signing_id, values(TeamId) as team_id, values(CsValidationCategory) as validation_category,
        values(SHA256HashData) as sha256
        by aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - last_seen

hazards.text: SigningId is a string the signer chose; a build signed as com.apple.anything by a Developer ID or ad hoc still reports it. TeamId '-' and CS_PLATFORM_BINARY in CodeSigningFlags are what say Apple signed it; the known-good corpus checks the hash and path behind the name.
Apple signed means CsValidationCategory 1 with TeamId '-', as the sensor reports its own mac process events. A sensor build that reports neither field shows every mac process here.

The window is inside the search text, so the saved search keeps it whatever the schedule dialog says. Match the schedule to it (a seven-day window every day repeats rows; a one-day window every day does not).
index=`cs_index` is a macro: define it once (queries/macros) or replace it with your index.
Time bounds are on _time (index time); timestamp and ContextTimeStamp are sensor-side and differ.
